intro: In reports, research and serious emails, good writers rarely say '100% sure' unless they really are. Today you'll learn to soften a claim (tend to, it would appear that, arguably) and to show exactly how certain you are, from 'almost certainly' to 'there is little evidence that'. Warm-up: think of a claim you read in a report or a news story that sounded far too sure.
teachingNotes: Hedging (melunakkan klaim) = showing that a claim is not 100% certain or not true in every case, so the claim matches the evidence. Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b2-modals-deduction the learner knows the certainty scale for guesses (must have / might have / can't have); from b2-essay-writing and b2-discussion they know tend to, many / most / often instead of all / always, It could be argued that …, There's a good chance that …, I suspect …. Today is vocabulary for academic and professional writing. Softeners: tend to + base verb (cenderung), appear to / seem to (tampaknya; appear is a bit more formal), it would appear that / it appears that / it seems that (would here is just softer, not a condition: a phrase to remember), arguably (bisa dibilang: marks a claim as an opinion you can defend, often with a superlative: arguably the best), to some extent (sampai batas tertentu), in some cases (dalam beberapa kasus), may / might / could contribute to (bisa ikut menyebabkan), suggests / indicates (mengindikasikan / menunjukkan) instead of proves (membuktikan).

The node's common errors: *'This proves that social media causes depression' (for one survey) → This suggests that social media may contribute to depression. One study rarely proves anything, and a survey shows that two things happen together, not that one causes the other. And over-hedging: *'It may possibly perhaps be true' → It may be true. One hedge is enough; three make the writer sound unsure of everything. Be honest that experienced writers sometimes combine two (could perhaps, may possibly) but a clean report uses one. Also: *'They are tend to …' (from Indonesian 'mereka cenderung', where cenderung works like an adjective) → They tend to … (tend is a verb); *'tend to using' → tend to use; *'tends' with a plural subject. Two meanings of suggest: menyarankan (I suggest we start at nine) and mengindikasikan (The data suggests that …): today it's the second one.

Degrees of certainty, strongest to weakest: clearly / undoubtedly (jelas / tidak diragukan) → almost certainly (hampir pasti) → it is highly likely that (sangat mungkin) → probably / it is likely that (kemungkinan besar) → possibly / may (mungkin) → it is unlikely that (kemungkinan kecil) → there is little evidence that (hampir tidak ada bukti) → there is no evidence that (tidak ada bukti). Word position: almost certainly / probably go after will and be and before a main verb (Prices will probably rise; He is almost certainly right). likely is an adjective: It is likely that … / Prices are likely to rise, not *'It likely that'. 'will likely' is common in American English; British English prefers will probably / is likely to: accept both. little vs a little: There is little evidence = almost none (negative); There is a little evidence = some (positive). Treat the scale as a guide: probably and it is likely that are equal, and it is unlikely that / there is little evidence that are different kinds of statement. Only test clearly separated points (e.g. almost certainly > probably > possibly > unlikely).

Culture and the Indonesian bridge: cenderung = tend to, tampaknya = seem / appear to / it would appear that, kemungkinan besar = probably / it is likely that, bisa dibilang = arguably, hampir pasti = almost certainly, kemungkinan kecil = unlikely. In many Indonesian workplaces people soften a lot when they speak (mungkin, sepertinya, agak), yet reports and proposals often say pasti, terbukti or sangat efektif without data. English academic and professional readers expect the claim to match the evidence: absolute claims without evidence sound unscientific or like advertising. Present this respectfully as a habit to change in English reports, not as a criticism of Indonesian culture. Don't hedge known facts (The meeting is on Monday; Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands) or your own clear results.

At C1 much of this is style: how much a writer hedges depends on the field, the reader and the strength of the evidence. Accept reasonable alternatives (seem / appear, suggests / indicates, may / might / could) and only mark clear cases wrong: a too-strong verb (proves, clearly) for weak evidence, a pile of hedges, the wrong grammar (are tend to, it likely that), or a certainty word on the wrong side of the scale. When the learner writes a paragraph, check first whether each claim matches its evidence, then correct one or two words.

Limits: A0–B2 grammar only. No inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive or impersonal passives as a topic ('It is thought that …', 'is believed to have …'); avoid perfect infinitives ('appears to have increased'): if a learner meets one, call it a phrase to remember. It is likely that …, It would appear that … and It could be argued that … are taught as fixed phrases. Contexts: university research, ministries and NGOs, startups, banks, HR reports, market forecasts in rupiah, transport in Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya and Yogyakarta. Keep facts general and safe; don't invent statistics about real organisations.

keyPoints.title: Soften a claim so it matches the evidence
keyPoints.explanation: Hedging means softening a claim: not 100% sure, not true in every case. Use tend to + base verb (cenderung), appear to / seem to (tampaknya), It would appear that … (a formal phrase), arguably (bisa dibilang, for an opinion you can defend), to some extent and in some cases (limits), and may / might / could contribute to instead of causes. For one study, say suggests or indicates, not proves. One hedge is enough: not 'may possibly perhaps'. tend is a verb: They tend to …, not 'They are tend to'.

examples.en: Junior staff tend to stay late before a deadline.
examples.id: Staf junior cenderung pulang terlambat menjelang tenggat.

examples.en: The survey suggests that long meetings may reduce productivity.
examples.id: Survei itu mengindikasikan bahwa rapat yang panjang bisa menurunkan produktivitas.

examples.en: Arguably, Bandung has the most creative startup scene in Indonesia.
examples.id: Bisa dibilang, Bandung punya ekosistem startup paling kreatif di Indonesia.

id.title: Melunakkan klaim supaya sesuai dengan buktinya
id.explanation: Hedging berarti melunakkan klaim: tidak 100% yakin, tidak berlaku di semua kasus. Pakai tend to + kata kerja dasar (cenderung), appear to / seem to (tampaknya), It would appear that … (frasa formal), arguably (bisa dibilang, untuk pendapat yang bisa kamu pertahankan), to some extent dan in some cases (membatasi klaim), dan may / might / could contribute to (bisa ikut menyebabkan) sebagai ganti causes. Untuk satu penelitian, pakai suggests atau indicates (mengindikasikan), bukan proves (membuktikan). Satu hedge sudah cukup: bukan 'may possibly perhaps'. tend adalah kata kerja: They tend to …, bukan 'They are tend to'.

keyPoints.title: Show exactly how certain you are
keyPoints.explanation: From strongest to weakest: clearly / undoubtedly → almost certainly → it is highly likely that → probably / it is likely that → possibly / may → it is unlikely that → there is little evidence that → there is no evidence that. almost certainly and probably go after will / be and before the main verb: Prices will probably rise. likely is an adjective: It is likely that … or Prices are likely to rise. Careful: There is little evidence = almost none; There is a little evidence = some.

examples.en: The new toll road will almost certainly reduce travel time to the airport.
examples.id: Jalan tol baru itu hampir pasti mengurangi waktu tempuh ke bandara.

examples.en: It is likely that demand will fall after the holiday season.
examples.id: Kemungkinan besar permintaan akan turun setelah musim liburan.

examples.en: There is little evidence that the new logo increased sales.
examples.id: Hampir tidak ada bukti bahwa logo baru itu meningkatkan penjualan.

id.title: Menunjukkan seberapa yakin kamu, dengan tepat
id.explanation: Dari yang paling kuat ke yang paling lemah: clearly / undoubtedly (jelas / tidak diragukan) → almost certainly (hampir pasti) → it is highly likely that (sangat mungkin) → probably / it is likely that (kemungkinan besar) → possibly / may (mungkin) → it is unlikely that (kemungkinan kecil) → there is little evidence that (hampir tidak ada bukti) → there is no evidence that (tidak ada bukti). almost certainly dan probably diletakkan setelah will / be dan sebelum kata kerja utama: Prices will probably rise. likely adalah kata sifat: It is likely that … atau Prices are likely to rise. Hati-hati: There is little evidence = hampir tidak ada bukti; There is a little evidence = ada sedikit bukti.

expected: junior engineers tend to ask fewer questions in meetings

assessment.prompt: A survey of 300 nurses in Surabaya found that nurses on night shifts reported worse sleep. Complete the report with one verb: The survey ___ that night shifts may affect sleep quality, although it does not prove it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: suggests / indicates (mengindikasikan): one survey gives a sign, not proof. 'shows' = 60 (stronger than one survey allows, and it clashes with 'does not prove it'). 'suggested' / 'indicated' = 80 (right word, but the rest of the sentence is in the present). 'suggest' without -s = 70 (survey is singular). 'proves' = 0 (the sentence itself says it does not prove it).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: In Bu Ani's data, small online shops ___ (cenderung) to grow faster than large ones, although there are many exceptions.
assessment.rubric: Correct: tend (tend to + base verb = cenderung; a general pattern with exceptions). 'seem' / 'appear' = 70 (a correct hedge, but it means tampaknya, not cenderung). 'tends' = 50 (shops is plural). 'are tend' = 30 (copies Indonesian 'cenderung' as an adjective: tend is a verb).

assessment.prompt: Dimas's supervisor says this sentence has too many hedges. Rewrite it with only ONE hedge word: The new bus lane may possibly perhaps reduce traffic on Jalan Sudirman.
acceptableAnswers: the new bus lane may reduce traffic on jalan sudirman
the new bus lane might reduce traffic on jalan sudirman
the new bus lane could reduce traffic on jalan sudirman
the new bus lane will possibly reduce traffic on jalan sudirman
perhaps the new bus lane will reduce traffic on jalan sudirman
the new bus lane may reduce traffic on sudirman
the new bus lane might reduce traffic on sudirman
the new bus lane could reduce traffic on sudirman
assessment.rubric: Correct: one hedge only: The new bus lane may / might / could reduce traffic on Jalan Sudirman (or 'will possibly', 'Perhaps … will'). Changing the strength ('will probably') = 80 (one hedge, but stronger than the original). Two hedges left ('may possibly reduce') = 50 (better, but still more than needed). No hedge at all ('The new bus lane reduces / will reduce traffic') = 40 (too strong: the supervisor only asked to remove the extra hedges). 'may possibly perhaps' unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: ___ (bisa dibilang), Yogyakarta is the best city in Indonesia for students: it is affordable, safe and full of universities. Not everyone agrees, of course.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Arguably (bisa dibilang: an opinion you can defend with reasons, not a proven fact). 'Probably' / 'Possibly' = 50 (they talk about how likely a fact is, not about an opinion). 'Clearly' / 'Undoubtedly' = 0 (the opposite: 'Not everyone agrees'). Spelling error that keeps the word clear ('arguabley') = 80.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: The final figures aren't ready yet, but it is ___ (kemungkinan besar) that the project will cost more than Rp 2 billion.
assessment.rubric: Correct: likely (it is likely that = kemungkinan besar); 'probable' is also accepted (more formal). 'highly likely' = 100 (two words, but a stronger, correct choice). 'possible' = 50 (that's mungkin, weaker than kemungkinan besar). 'probably' = 30 (an adverb: 'it is probably that' is wrong). 'certain' = 20 (too strong: the figures aren't ready).

assessment.prompt: Many parents believe that video games make children violent. Most large studies, however, have found no clear link. Complete with one word: There is ___ evidence that video games cause violent behaviour.
assessment.rubric: Correct: little (= almost no evidence; hampir tidak ada bukti); limited / weak / insufficient / scant are also accepted. 'no' = 70 (understandable, but 'most' studies, not all, so 'little' is more accurate). 'a little' = 20 (it means there is SOME evidence: the opposite message). 'some' / 'strong' = 0 (the studies found no clear link).

assessment.prompt: Ticket sales are very low and the main sponsor has pulled out. Complete with one word: It is ___ (kemungkinan kecil) that the festival in Bali will go ahead next month.
assessment.rubric: Correct: unlikely (it is unlikely that = kemungkinan kecil); improbable and doubtful are also accepted. 'not likely' = 90 (two words, same meaning). 'impossible' = 40 (too strong: there is still a small chance). 'likely' = 0 (the opposite).

material.title: What is hedging, and why do English reports need it?

id.title: Apa itu hedging, dan kenapa laporan berbahasa Inggris membutuhkannya?

blocks.text:
**Hedging** means softening a **claim** (klaim: a statement that something is true). You show that you are not 100% sure, or that it isn't true in every case. The goal is not to sound weak: the goal is that **the claim matches the evidence**.

You already know some of this. In B2 you guessed about the past with **must have / might have / can't have**, you wrote **many** or **most** instead of *all*, and you used **tend to**, **It could be argued that …** and **There's a good chance that …**. Now you'll add the vocabulary that academic and professional English uses every day.

Compare:
- Too strong: *Working from home makes employees more productive.* (Always? Everyone? Says who?)
- Hedged: **Working from home appears to make some employees more productive.**

id.text:
**Hedging** artinya melunakkan sebuah **klaim** (claim: pernyataan bahwa sesuatu itu benar). Kamu menunjukkan bahwa kamu tidak 100% yakin, atau bahwa hal itu tidak berlaku di semua kasus. Tujuannya bukan supaya terdengar lemah, tapi supaya **klaimnya sesuai dengan buktinya**.

Sebagian sudah kamu kenal. Di B2 kamu menebak masa lalu dengan **must have / might have / can't have**, menulis **many** atau **most** sebagai ganti *all*, dan memakai **tend to**, **It could be argued that …** dan **There's a good chance that …**. Sekarang kamu menambah kosakata yang dipakai setiap hari dalam bahasa Inggris akademik dan profesional.

Bandingkan:
- Terlalu kuat: *Working from home makes employees more productive.* (Selalu? Semua orang? Kata siapa?)
- Dengan hedging: **Working from home appears to make some employees more productive.**

blocks.text:
**A habit to change in English reports.** In many Indonesian offices, people soften a lot when they *speak*: *mungkin*, *sepertinya*, *agak kurang*. But reports and proposals often say *pasti*, *terbukti* or *sangat efektif* with little data behind them. English readers, especially in universities, ministries, NGOs and international companies, read it the other way round: a claim that sounds 100% sure without strong evidence sounds **unscientific** or like an advertisement, and they trust the writer less. In an English report, keep *pasti* and *terbukti* for things you can really prove.

But **don't hedge facts**: *The meeting is on Monday.* *Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands.* Hedging a clear fact makes you sound unsure of everything.

id.text:
**Kebiasaan yang perlu diubah di laporan berbahasa Inggris.** Di banyak kantor di Indonesia, orang sangat melunakkan ucapan saat *berbicara*: *mungkin*, *sepertinya*, *agak kurang*. Tapi laporan dan proposal sering menulis *pasti*, *terbukti* atau *sangat efektif* dengan data yang sedikit. Pembaca berbahasa Inggris, terutama di kampus, kementerian, LSM dan perusahaan internasional, melihatnya terbalik: klaim yang terdengar 100% yakin tanpa bukti kuat terdengar **tidak ilmiah** atau seperti iklan, dan mereka jadi kurang percaya pada penulisnya. Di laporan berbahasa Inggris, simpan *pasti* dan *terbukti* untuk hal yang benar-benar bisa kamu buktikan.

Tapi **jangan melunakkan fakta**: *The meeting is on Monday.* *Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands.* Kalau fakta yang jelas pun kamu lunakkan, kamu terdengar ragu tentang semuanya.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence should NOT be hedged?
options: The quarterly meeting is on Monday at 9 a.m.
blocks.explain: The meeting time is a known fact, so you just state it. The other two are general claims about cause and effect: you'd need strong evidence to say them without a hedge (for example 'Online classes may improve some students' grades').

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang TIDAK perlu dilunakkan?
id.explain: Jadwal rapat adalah fakta yang sudah pasti, jadi cukup disebutkan saja. Dua kalimat lainnya adalah klaim umum tentang sebab-akibat: kamu butuh bukti kuat untuk menulisnya tanpa hedging (misalnya 'Online classes may improve some students' grades').

material.title: The softening toolkit: tend to, appear to, arguably

id.title: Perangkat pelunak: tend to, appear to, arguably

blocks.text:
**1. It's a general pattern, with exceptions**
- **tend to** + base verb (cenderung): *Young professionals tend to rent rather than buy.* Negative: **tend not to** (formal) or **don't tend to**.
- **in some cases** (dalam beberapa kasus), **in many cases**, **often**: *In some cases, the app crashes on older phones.*
- **to some extent** (sampai batas tertentu): *The campaign worked to some extent.*

**2. It looks true, but you're not sure**
- **appear to / seem to** + verb (tampaknya): *The figures appear to be wrong.* **appear** is a little more formal than **seem**.
- **It appears that … / It seems that … / It would appear that …** (tampaknya): *It would appear that the client has changed its mind.* Here **would** doesn't mean 'if': it just makes the phrase softer and more formal. Learn it as a phrase.

**3. It's your opinion, and you can defend it**
- **arguably** (bisa dibilang): *Arguably, this is the best policy we have.* It says 'I can give good reasons for this, but others may disagree.' It often goes with words like *the best*, *the most*, *the biggest*.

id.text:
**1. Pola umum, tapi ada pengecualian**
- **tend to** + kata kerja dasar (cenderung): *Young professionals tend to rent rather than buy.* Bentuk negatif: **tend not to** (formal) atau **don't tend to**.
- **in some cases** (dalam beberapa kasus), **in many cases**, **often**: *In some cases, the app crashes on older phones.*
- **to some extent** (sampai batas tertentu): *The campaign worked to some extent.*

**2. Kelihatannya benar, tapi kamu belum yakin**
- **appear to / seem to** + kata kerja (tampaknya): *The figures appear to be wrong.* **appear** sedikit lebih formal daripada **seem**.
- **It appears that … / It seems that … / It would appear that …** (tampaknya): *It would appear that the client has changed its mind.* Di sini **would** tidak berarti 'kalau': kata itu hanya membuat frasanya lebih lunak dan lebih formal. Hafalkan sebagai frasa.

**3. Ini pendapatmu, dan kamu bisa mempertahankannya**
- **arguably** (bisa dibilang): *Arguably, this is the best policy we have.* Artinya 'Saya bisa memberi alasan yang bagus untuk ini, tapi orang lain mungkin tidak setuju.' Sering dipakai dengan kata seperti *the best*, *the most*, *the biggest*.

blocks.text: **The 'cenderung' trap.** In Indonesian, *cenderung* behaves like an adjective (*mereka cenderung pendiam*), so learners write *'They are tend to be quiet.'* In English, **tend** is a **verb** (kata kerja): **They tend to be quiet.** No *are*, and the verb after it stays in its base form: *tend to use*, not *'tend to using'*. With *he / she / it*: **She tends to …**

id.text: **Jebakan 'cenderung'.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *cenderung* berperilaku seperti kata sifat (*mereka cenderung pendiam*), jadi orang sering menulis *'They are tend to be quiet.'* Dalam bahasa Inggris, **tend** adalah **kata kerja** (verb): **They tend to be quiet.** Tidak pakai *are*, dan kata kerja sesudahnya tetap bentuk dasar: *tend to use*, bukan *'tend to using'*. Dengan *he / she / it*: **She tends to …**

blocks.explain: tend is a verb, so no 'are': tend to + base verb (pay). 'tend to be pay' adds an extra verb that doesn't fit.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Customers in smaller cities ___ pay by bank transfer rather than by card.
id.explain: tend adalah kata kerja, jadi tidak pakai 'are': tend to + kata kerja dasar (pay). 'tend to be pay' menambah kata kerja yang tidak cocok.

material.title: Not too strong, not too weak: proves vs suggests

id.title: Tidak terlalu kuat, tidak terlalu lemah: proves vs suggests

blocks.text:
Choose the verb that matches what the evidence can really do:
- **proves** (membuktikan): only for very strong, final evidence. One study almost never *proves* anything.
- **shows / demonstrates** (menunjukkan): clear, strong evidence.
- **indicates** (menunjukkan, mengindikasikan): it points in that direction.
- **suggests** (mengindikasikan): there is a sign, but more research is needed.

**suggest has two meanings.** *I suggest we start at nine* = menyarankan. *The data suggests that …* = mengindikasikan. In reports, it's often the second one.

**Cause or connection?** A survey can find that two things happen together (people who use social media a lot also feel sad more often). That does **not** show that one *causes* the other. So say **may contribute to** (bisa ikut menyebabkan) or **is linked to** (berkaitan dengan), not *causes*.

id.text:
Pilih kata kerja yang sesuai dengan apa yang benar-benar bisa ditunjukkan buktinya:
- **proves** (membuktikan): hanya untuk bukti yang sangat kuat dan final. Satu penelitian hampir tidak pernah *membuktikan* apa pun.
- **shows / demonstrates** (menunjukkan): bukti yang jelas dan kuat.
- **indicates** (menunjukkan, mengindikasikan): mengarah ke sana.
- **suggests** (mengindikasikan): ada tanda-tandanya, tapi masih perlu riset lebih lanjut.

**suggest punya dua arti.** *I suggest we start at nine* = menyarankan. *The data suggests that …* = mengindikasikan. Di laporan, biasanya arti yang kedua.

**Sebab atau hubungan?** Survei bisa menemukan bahwa dua hal terjadi bersamaan (orang yang sering main media sosial juga lebih sering merasa sedih). Itu **tidak** menunjukkan bahwa yang satu *menyebabkan* yang lain. Jadi pakai **may contribute to** (bisa ikut menyebabkan) atau **is linked to** (berkaitan dengan), bukan *causes*.

rows.en: This proves that social media causes depression.
rows.id: Ini membuktikan bahwa media sosial menyebabkan depresi.
rows.note: ✗ for one survey: far too strong

rows.en: This suggests that social media may contribute to depression.
rows.id: Ini mengindikasikan bahwa media sosial bisa ikut menyebabkan depresi.

rows.en: It may possibly perhaps be true.
rows.id: Itu mungkin barangkali bisa jadi benar.

blocks.text:
**Over-hedging is a mistake too.** If every sentence has *may possibly perhaps*, the reader can't tell what you actually think, and you sound unsure of your own work. Use **one** hedge per claim, and only where the evidence is uncertain. (Experienced writers sometimes use two, like *could perhaps*, but three is always too many.)

This is partly style: different fields and readers expect different amounts. The safe rule for a report: **strong evidence → strong verb; weak or one-study evidence → one hedge.**

id.text:
**Terlalu banyak pelunak juga kesalahan.** Kalau setiap kalimat berisi *may possibly perhaps*, pembaca tidak tahu apa yang sebenarnya kamu pikirkan, dan kamu terdengar ragu dengan hasil kerjamu sendiri. Pakai **satu** pelunak per klaim, dan hanya kalau buktinya memang belum pasti. (Penulis berpengalaman kadang memakai dua, seperti *could perhaps*, tapi tiga selalu terlalu banyak.)

Ini sebagian soal gaya: bidang dan pembaca yang berbeda mengharapkan kadar yang berbeda. Aturan aman untuk laporan: **bukti kuat → kata kerja kuat; bukti lemah atau satu penelitian → satu pelunak.**

blocks.prompt: A start-up asked 60 of its own users whether its app saves time, and most said yes. Which sentence fits the company's report?
options: The results demonstrate that the app saves every user time.
The results indicate that many users feel the app saves them time.
The results might possibly perhaps indicate that the app could save time.
blocks.explain: 60 of its own users is a small sample, so 'demonstrate' and 'every user' are too strong. The third sentence piles up three hedges. 'indicate' + 'many users feel' matches the evidence.

id.prompt: Sebuah startup bertanya kepada 60 penggunanya sendiri apakah aplikasinya menghemat waktu, dan sebagian besar menjawab ya. Kalimat mana yang cocok untuk laporan perusahaan itu?
id.explain: 60 pengguna sendiri adalah sampel kecil, jadi 'demonstrate' dan 'every user' terlalu kuat. Kalimat ketiga menumpuk tiga pelunak. 'indicate' + 'many users feel' sesuai dengan buktinya.

material.title: How sure are you? The certainty scale

blocks.text:
From the strongest to the weakest:
- **clearly / undoubtedly** (jelas / tidak diragukan lagi): only with very strong evidence
- **almost certainly** (hampir pasti)
- **it is highly likely that** (sangat mungkin, kemungkinannya sangat besar)
- **probably / it is likely that** (kemungkinan besar)
- **possibly / may / might / could** (mungkin)
- **it is unlikely that** (kemungkinan kecil)
- **there is little evidence that** (hampir tidak ada bukti bahwa)
- **there is no evidence that** (tidak ada bukti bahwa)

Where do they go?
- **almost certainly** and **probably** go after *will* / *be* and before the main verb: *Prices **will probably** rise.* *She **is almost certainly** right.*
- **likely** is an adjective (kata sifat), so it needs *be*: **It is likely that** prices will rise. / Prices **are likely to** rise. Not *'It likely that …'*.

The scale is a guide, not a ruler: *probably* and *it is likely that* mean the same, and the last three talk about evidence rather than chance.

id.text:
Dari yang paling kuat ke yang paling lemah:
- **clearly / undoubtedly** (jelas / tidak diragukan lagi): hanya dengan bukti yang sangat kuat
- **almost certainly** (hampir pasti)
- **it is highly likely that** (sangat mungkin, kemungkinannya sangat besar)
- **probably / it is likely that** (kemungkinan besar)
- **possibly / may / might / could** (mungkin)
- **it is unlikely that** (kemungkinan kecil)
- **there is little evidence that** (hampir tidak ada bukti bahwa)
- **there is no evidence that** (tidak ada bukti bahwa)

Letaknya di mana?
- **almost certainly** dan **probably** diletakkan setelah *will* / *be* dan sebelum kata kerja utama: *Prices **will probably** rise.* *She **is almost certainly** right.*
- **likely** adalah kata sifat (adjective), jadi butuh *be*: **It is likely that** prices will rise. / Prices **are likely to** rise. Bukan *'It likely that …'*.

Skala ini panduan, bukan penggaris: *probably* dan *it is likely that* artinya sama, dan tiga yang terakhir membicarakan bukti, bukan peluang.

rows.en: The new MRT line will almost certainly open later than planned.
rows.id: Jalur MRT baru itu hampir pasti dibuka lebih lambat dari rencana.

rows.en: It is highly likely that the board will approve the budget.
rows.id: Sangat mungkin dewan direksi akan menyetujui anggaran itu.

rows.en: Rice prices are likely to rise before Lebaran.
rows.id: Harga beras kemungkinan besar naik menjelang Lebaran.

rows.en: It is unlikely that the client will sign before Friday.
rows.id: Kemungkinan kecil klien itu akan tanda tangan sebelum hari Jumat.

rows.en: There is no evidence that the leak came from our office.
rows.id: Tidak ada bukti bahwa kebocoran itu berasal dari kantor kami.

blocks.text:
**little or a little? A tiny word, the opposite message.**
- **There is little evidence that …** = hampir tidak ada bukti (negative: the claim is weak).
- **There is a little evidence that …** = ada sedikit bukti (positive: some support).

**will likely** (*Prices will likely rise*) is very common in American English. British English usually prefers **will probably** or **are likely to**. Both are fine; just be consistent.

Indonesian *pasti* isn't always *certainly*: in speech, *pasti* is often a strong guess (*Dia pasti capek* = *She must be tired*). In a report, use **clearly** or **undoubtedly** only when the evidence really is that strong.

id.text:
**little atau a little? Kata kecil, pesan yang berlawanan.**
- **There is little evidence that …** = hampir tidak ada bukti (negatif: klaimnya lemah).
- **There is a little evidence that …** = ada sedikit bukti (positif: ada dukungan).

**will likely** (*Prices will likely rise*) sangat umum dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika. Bahasa Inggris Inggris (British) biasanya lebih memilih **will probably** atau **are likely to**. Dua-duanya boleh; yang penting konsisten.

*pasti* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak selalu *certainly*: dalam percakapan, *pasti* sering berarti tebakan yang kuat (*Dia pasti capek* = *She must be tired*). Di laporan, pakai **clearly** atau **undoubtedly** hanya kalau buktinya memang sekuat itu.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani's team tested a new payment page for six months. Only 3 of 400 customers said it was slower, and the other data shows no change in speed. Complete: There is ___ evidence that the new page is slower.
blocks.explain: Almost no evidence supports the claim, so 'little' (hampir tidak ada). 'a little' would say there is some support, the opposite message. 'strong' contradicts the data.

id.prompt: Tim Bu Ani menguji halaman pembayaran baru selama enam bulan. Hanya 3 dari 400 pelanggan yang bilang halamannya lebih lambat, dan data lainnya tidak menunjukkan perubahan kecepatan. Lengkapi: There is ___ evidence that the new page is slower.
id.explain: Hampir tidak ada bukti yang mendukung klaim itu, jadi 'little' (hampir tidak ada). 'a little' berarti ada sedikit dukungan, pesannya berlawanan. 'strong' bertentangan dengan datanya.

suggestedQuestions: Doesn't hedging make me sound weak or unsure?
Is 'little evidence' the same as 'a little evidence'?

resources.title: Hedging (cautious language) in Academic Writing
resources.note: A clear 13-minute video for university students: what hedging is, the main types (verbs like tend to and appear to, modal verbs, adverbs, adjectives) and how it looks in a real academic text. All in English; it also covers 'boosting', the opposite of hedging.

id.note: Video jelas sekitar 13 menit untuk mahasiswa: apa itu hedging, jenis-jenis utamanya (kata kerja seperti tend to dan appear to, modal, kata keterangan, kata sifat) dan contohnya di teks akademik asli. Seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris; juga membahas 'boosting', kebalikan dari hedging.

resources.title: Hedging Language - Academic Writing
resources.note: A walk through hedging language group by group (introductory verbs, adverbs of frequency, modal verbs, adjectives, adverbs and nouns, that-clauses), ending with an exercise. All in English, for students preparing for university.

resources.title: Writing Features: Hedging

id.intro: Di laporan, riset dan email yang serius, penulis yang baik jarang bilang '100% yakin' kecuali memang benar-benar yakin. Hari ini kamu belajar melunakkan klaim (tend to, it would appear that, arguably) dan menunjukkan dengan tepat seberapa yakin kamu, dari 'almost certainly' sampai 'there is little evidence that'. Pemanasan: ingat satu klaim yang pernah kamu baca di laporan atau berita yang terdengar terlalu yakin.
suggestedQuestions: Apakah hedging tidak membuat saya terdengar lemah atau ragu?
Apakah 'little evidence' sama dengan 'a little evidence'?

assessment.hd-1: Sebuah survei terhadap 300 perawat di Surabaya menemukan bahwa perawat shift malam melaporkan tidur yang lebih buruk. Lengkapi laporannya dengan satu kata kerja: The survey ___ that night shifts may affect sleep quality, although it does not prove it.
assessment.hd-2: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: In Bu Ani's data, small online shops ___ (cenderung) to grow faster than large ones, although there are many exceptions.
assessment.hd-3: Atasan Dimas bilang kalimat ini punya terlalu banyak pelunak. Tulis ulang dengan hanya SATU kata pelunak: The new bus lane may possibly perhaps reduce traffic on Jalan Sudirman.
assessment.hd-4: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: ___ (bisa dibilang), Yogyakarta is the best city in Indonesia for students: it is affordable, safe and full of universities. Not everyone agrees, of course.
assessment.hd-5: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: The final figures aren't ready yet, but it is ___ (kemungkinan besar) that the project will cost more than Rp 2 billion.
assessment.hd-6: Banyak orang tua percaya bahwa video game membuat anak-anak jadi kasar. Namun, sebagian besar penelitian besar tidak menemukan hubungan yang jelas. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: There is ___ evidence that video games cause violent behaviour.
assessment.hd-7: Penjualan tiket sangat rendah dan sponsor utama sudah mundur. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: It is ___ (kemungkinan kecil) that the festival in Bali will go ahead next month.
